pieces.title: Prelude I · Praeludium per omnes tonos
pieces.notes:
BWV 846's broken chords climb through all 24 keys in the WTC's own order, C, c, C#, c#, D, d and on to b, then home. In every minor key the Neapolitan chord (bII) becomes the next major tonic, a semitone up.

It is voiced as a Shepard-Risset illusion: each note sounds in several octaves under a fixed loudness curve, so the music rises a semitone with every key and yet arrives back in C at the register where it began. C minor opens with the Royal Theme of the Musical Offering. E-flat minor is the darkest point; the climax is a pedal in G-sharp minor; A major is the loudest bar.

At the da capo the fugue subject floats above Bach's own bars at half speed, the way Gounod laid a melody over this prelude. Try the meantone tuning: the remote keys sour, which is why the well-tempered keyboard existed.

pieces.title: Fugue I · Scala strettarum (2 voices)
pieces.notes:
The subject was found by search so that it combines with itself in stretto at every distance from a whole bar down to a single eighth note. The fugue climbs that ladder one rung at a time: bar, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 and finally 1 eighth apart, through A minor, E minor, G, D minor, F and back to C.

Bach's own C-major subject (BWV 846) opens the piece alone in the bass and becomes the countersubject. It returns over the subject's augmentation in the coda, and B-A-C-H is the top line of the last cadence.

pieces.title: Prelude in C minor v3 (was 'Pair I')
pieces.notes: The previous version, kept for comparison. Mis-numbered: C minor is No. II in Bach's order, so its fugue needs three voices.

pieces.title: Fugue in C minor v5, 2 voices
pieces.notes: The previous version. Review found 15 of 34 bars with code-chosen pitches, 12 bars without a subject entry and a peak that was the thinnest bar.

pieces.title: Prelude IV v6
pieces.notes: The previous version. No root-position cadence on a strong beat; same metre and tempo as its fugue.

pieces.title: Fugue IV v7, 5 voices
pieces.notes: The previous version. 22 accented parallels the old checker missed; all five voices first sound together only at bar 33; the countersubject changes its pitches at every entry.

pieces.title: Prelude V v1
pieces.notes: The previous version. One 8-bar progression three times; pure arpeggio with no top line.

pieces.title: Fugue V v3, 6 voices
pieces.notes: The previous version. Every stretto collapses onto a held triad over a pedal; half the beats are D or A chords; 38 accented parallels.

pieces.title: Prelude VIII v1 (French overture)
pieces.notes: The previous version. It replaced the 12/8 'Night loom' prelude Sam liked.

pieces.title: Fugue VIII v3, 9 staves
pieces.notes: The previous version: in practice a four-voice fugue on nine staves, with a climax of the subject in octaves over block chords.

pieces.title: Fugue VIII, 100-bar procession
pieces.notes: The older chamber audition. The critic finds 220 parallel fifths and octaves, 195 unresolved dissonances and 286 low-register clashes, which likely explains the harmonies Sam heard as mistakes.
